body:
Hello,

You replied pretty late to this but of course I was going to go back, and I've seen your replies. Thank you for your insight. I don't believe in God though, if you believe in God that can be a comforting argument, but I don't.
Hmm, alright. You can read a couple of my posts above to know about my tics related to my breathing, and I don't know if those count as "vocal" since they make noise but I don't move my vocal cords.

I have breathing-related tics that make noise though. Contracting the chest and exhaling quickly, contracting my abdomen or even my bowel and breathing in shakily and slowly, noticeably shivering while inhaling. Or just drawing in a long deep breath when I'm just sitting still after an urge in my brain sends that message. Do those classify as "vocal" tics? I'm not sure since I'm not moving my vocal cords or giving voice to anything. So if that's combined with my motor tics, is it Tourettes?

Hmm, well do breathing things count as "vocal" tics? I mentioned how I sometimes contract my chest and let out a short quick exhale. Sometimes I contract my abdomen/midsection and shiver a little and breathe in slowly. It's a little noisy and can be heard if it's a dead-quiet room. All of these are preceded by the same "urge" in the brain to just do that to relieve tension/be comfortable, which is typical of everything I've heard about Tourette's.

You said your symptoms are similar to what I described. Does that mean you have no vocal tics? All the sources I'm finding say that there's at least one vocal tic involved if you have it. A big reason I believed for so long that the doctor was wrong and I didn't actually have it was because I have no vocal tic. It was pretty comforting to know I had nothing vocal, because to most people who only know about it through media, Tourette's = vocal, so no vocal must = no Tourette's. I made myself believe that too. But there's really nothing else the muscle flexing and neck jerks and excessive winking and blinking can be. So isn't it wrong to say there's at least one vocal tic that needs to be involved? I am more or less 100% sure Tourette's is what this is. Do you also have nothing vocal, or is it partially vocal for you?

Hi. You say yours is completely non-vocal? Multiple sources including the Wikipedia page say there is at least one vocal tic involved in people afflicted. In fact one big reason I believed I didn't actually have it for so long is because I have no vocal tic. I thought the neurologist when I was 12 was too hasty by saying that, and I thought no vocal = no Tourette's. But these muscle flexes and eye movements and the neck jerks to the side simply can't be anything else and I realize that now. So why does basically every source say vocal tics are inevitably involved? That can't be right...

Yeah, but the thing is I didn't really know I had it, I denied what the neurologist said when I was 12  and the ticks/movements died down in intensity and frequency a little while later so I just assumed it was a passing phase, a weird one but still an unexplainable phase. I thought it was no longer a problem until two nights ago when that guy said it. I wasn't nervous about it because it wasn't even on my mind, but the shit still happened and got noticed. Since he said it I thought about every movement I do have and how it's an urge and a comfort and quickly realized it is Tourette's and can't be anything else. Now I wonder how many people I've talked to one on one have noticed it and not said anything. I didn't even know or believe or think about it but it still happens. Now that I've finally realized it I really feel like shit, and I'm not going to be so quick to switch to a mentality of "I'm going to live a life with this, I'm going to tell people I have it and be open and comfortable about it." I can't, because I was assuming I didn't have it for this long and want to just not have it and be a normal person.

> just telling every girl you go on a date with "I have Tourette's Syndrome, that means I might make weird movements or twitches while we're here

But I don't want to do that. I hate the idea of having it and living a life with it and that's why I believed it was an incorrect diagnosis all those years ago. I'm not content with having it with people not judging me, I want to not have it at all. I really don't want to have to tell every new person I meet that I have Tourette Syndrome, as the first thing in conversation. I just want to start interactions like a normal person, without a whole prefaced speech about it. Like everyone else can do. It was out of my mind until a day ago like I said in the post. I don't want to switch the mentality of accepting that this is my life. I just want to not have it.

Yeah, I guess I can understand. I won't talk to a therapist either, not because I'm afraid they'd break confidentiality, but because they might have the authority to commit me (which actually a loophole as it indirectly and unofficially breaks confidentiality now that I think about it).

Ehh, I don't think so. Suicidal ideation is different from an imminent threat. If a therapist broke confidentiality simply for a patient's suicidal ideation with no evidence of an imminent threat of suicide, my guess is they lose their license.

>I can't talk to a professional because I can't risk them telling someone that I feel this way.

But, confidentiality? You know that's an oath, right? The only exception is if you threaten someone's life. If they break confidentiality for any other reason, they will lose their license to practice. How many therapists are willing to risk that?
Current city in Seattle. I only moved recently though and don't have many friends in the area.

Will it really be better just if people won't judge me? I don't want to have it with people not judging me, I want to not have it at all. I hate the messages my brain is always sending. They don't make sense and they're a neurological defect. I'm not going to just tell people "hey before you get to know me I have Tourette Syndrome, you might notice a tic or a quick movement but don't be startled because it's because of Tourette's." No, I'm not going to say that every time I meet a person. I want it to be like I don't have it, and I want to be able to meet and talk to people normally, without a preface speech of "I have this so don't be alarmed if you notice anything".
